description: Study of equations involving derivatives. Covers first-order and second-order ODEs, systems of differential equations, Laplace transforms, and series solutions, with applications to science and engineering.

concepts.title: Classification and Terminology
learning_objectives: Classify differential equations by order, linearity, and type (ODE vs PDE)
Identify the dependent and independent variables in a differential equation
Verify that a given function is a solution to a differential equation

concepts.title: Direction Fields and Solution Curves
learning_objectives: Sketch direction (slope) fields for first-order ODEs
Trace solution curves through the direction field from given initial conditions
Identify equilibrium solutions from a direction field

concepts.title: Existence and Uniqueness Theorem
learning_objectives: State the Picard-Lindelof existence and uniqueness theorem for first-order IVPs
Identify conditions under which uniqueness may fail
Apply the theorem to determine whether a given IVP has a unique solution

concepts.title: Separable Equations
learning_objectives: Identify and solve separable differential equations by separation of variables
Handle implicit solutions and determine explicit solutions when possible
Solve initial value problems for separable equations

concepts.title: First-Order Linear Equations
learning_objectives: Identify first-order linear equations in standard form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x)
Solve using the integrating factor method
Solve initial value problems for first-order linear equations

concepts.title: Exact Equations
learning_objectives: Determine whether M dx + N dy = 0 is exact using the exactness condition ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x
Solve exact differential equations by finding the potential function
Find integrating factors to convert non-exact equations to exact form

concepts.title: Substitution Methods
learning_objectives: Solve homogeneous first-order equations using the substitution v = y/x
Solve Bernoulli equations using the substitution w = y^{1−n}
Identify which substitution technique applies to a given equation

concepts.title: Growth, Decay, and Mixing Models
learning_objectives: Model exponential growth and decay with dy/dt = ky
Model logistic growth and determine carrying capacity and inflection point
Set up and solve mixing problems involving inflow and outflow rates

concepts.title: Newton's Law of Cooling and Other Models
learning_objectives: Model temperature change with Newton's law of cooling dT/dt = k(T − Tₑ)
Model simple electric circuits (RC circuits) with first-order linear ODEs
Set up and solve free-fall with air resistance as a first-order ODE

concepts.title: Numerical Methods: Euler's Method
learning_objectives: Apply Euler's method to approximate solutions of first-order IVPs
Analyze the effect of step size on the accuracy of Euler's method
Apply the improved Euler method (Heun's method) for better accuracy

concepts.title: Homogeneous Equations with Constant Coefficients
learning_objectives: Solve ay'' + by' + cy = 0 by finding roots of the characteristic equation
Handle distinct real, repeated real, and complex conjugate roots
Write the general solution using appropriate basis functions (exponentials, sines, cosines)

concepts.title: The Wronskian and Linear Independence
learning_objectives: Compute the Wronskian of two solutions
Use the Wronskian to test for linear independence of solutions
Apply Abel's theorem to relate the Wronskian to the coefficients of the ODE

concepts.title: Nonhomogeneous Equations: Undetermined Coefficients
learning_objectives: Identify the structure of a particular solution based on the forcing function
Apply the method of undetermined coefficients for polynomial, exponential, and sinusoidal forcing
Handle cases where the particular solution form duplicates a homogeneous solution

concepts.title: Nonhomogeneous Equations: Variation of Parameters
learning_objectives: Derive the variation of parameters formulas for second-order linear ODEs
Apply variation of parameters to solve equations with arbitrary forcing functions
Compare undetermined coefficients and variation of parameters in terms of applicability

concepts.title: Free Vibrations: Mass-Spring Systems
learning_objectives: Derive the equation of motion for a mass-spring system from Newton's second law
Solve undamped, underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped free vibration problems
Express solutions in amplitude-phase form and interpret physical behavior

concepts.title: Forced Vibrations and Resonance
learning_objectives: Solve forced oscillation problems with sinusoidal driving forces
Identify and analyze resonance when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency
Analyze steady-state and transient responses in damped forced systems

concepts.title: Electric Circuit Models (RLC Circuits)
learning_objectives: Derive the ODE governing a series RLC circuit using Kirchhoff's voltage law
Solve for current and charge in free and forced RLC circuits
Draw the analogy between mechanical and electrical oscillating systems

concepts.title: Definition and Properties of the Laplace Transform
learning_objectives: Compute Laplace transforms using the definition L{f(t)} = ∫₀^∞ e^{−st} f(t) dt
Apply linearity and the transforms of elementary functions (eᵃᵗ, tⁿ, sin, cos)
Apply the first and second shifting theorems

concepts.title: Inverse Laplace Transform and Partial Fractions
learning_objectives: Compute inverse Laplace transforms using tables and partial fraction decomposition
Apply the convolution theorem to find inverse transforms
Handle transforms involving s-shifting and t-shifting

concepts.title: Solving IVPs with the Laplace Transform
learning_objectives: Transform an ODE initial value problem into an algebraic equation in s
Solve second-order constant-coefficient IVPs using Laplace transforms
Handle discontinuous forcing functions using the unit step function

concepts.title: The Dirac Delta Function
learning_objectives: Define the Dirac delta function as a limit of unit impulse functions
Compute the Laplace transform of the delta function
Solve IVPs with impulsive forcing using delta functions

concepts.title: Introduction to Systems and Phase Portraits
learning_objectives: Convert a higher-order ODE to a system of first-order ODEs
Sketch phase portraits for two-dimensional linear systems
Classify equilibrium points from the phase portrait

concepts.title: Solving Linear Systems with Eigenvalues
learning_objectives: Solve 2×2 homogeneous linear systems x' = Ax using eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Handle real distinct, complex, and repeated eigenvalue cases
Classify equilibrium points as nodes, spirals, or saddles based on eigenvalue type

concepts.title: Nonlinear Systems and Stability
learning_objectives: Find equilibrium points of nonlinear autonomous systems
Linearize a nonlinear system at an equilibrium point using the Jacobian
Assess stability of equilibrium points using eigenvalues of the Jacobian

concepts.title: Power Series Solutions Near Ordinary Points
learning_objectives: Assume a power series solution y = Σ aₙ xⁿ and derive a recurrence relation for the coefficients
Find the radius of convergence of the series solution
Solve second-order ODEs near ordinary points using power series

concepts.title: Series Solutions Near Regular Singular Points (Frobenius Method)
learning_objectives: Classify singular points as regular or irregular
Apply the method of Frobenius to find series solutions y = xʳ Σ aₙ xⁿ
Determine the indicial equation and handle cases of equal and differing roots

concepts.title: Bessel Functions and Legendre Polynomials
learning_objectives: Derive Bessel's equation and identify Bessel functions of the first and second kind
Derive Legendre's equation and identify Legendre polynomials
Recognize the role of these special functions in physics and engineering applications

projects.title: Predator-Prey Dynamics (Lotka-Volterra)
projects.description: Model a predator-prey ecosystem using the Lotka-Volterra system. Analyze equilibria, linearize, classify stability, and numerically simulate population oscillations over time.
learning_objectives: Set up a nonlinear system of ODEs from a biological model
Linearize around equilibria and classify their stability
Numerically simulate trajectories and interpret phase portraits

projects.title: Designing a Shock Absorber
projects.description: Model a car suspension as a mass-spring-damper system. Determine the damping coefficient that achieves critical damping, then analyze the forced response to a sinusoidal road surface.
learning_objectives: Derive and solve the ODE for a mass-spring-damper system
Determine critical damping parameters analytically
Analyze the steady-state response amplitude as a function of driving frequency

projects.title: Solving an RLC Circuit with Laplace Transforms
projects.description: Analyze the transient and steady-state response of a series RLC circuit driven by a piecewise-constant voltage. Use the Laplace transform with step functions to handle the discontinuous input.
learning_objectives: Model a physical circuit as a second-order ODE with discontinuous forcing
Apply Laplace transform techniques including the unit step function
Interpret the solution in terms of transient decay and steady-state oscillation
